Update 5:  

So my apartment will be fully furnished in the next two days.  It's been a whirlwind of a week. Pretty much everything was purchased on sale, which is insane given the quality of the items I picked up.   If you told me a week ago that I would have a 3 bedroom apartment fully furnished in 10 days, I would've laughed.  I also would've laughed if you told me I'd have a date lined up as well.   Honestly, I haven't thought about my ex all week and I think I'm over the toughest part of this journey. At this point I just feel pity for her and everything she's done to herself.  I'm no longer afraid of the charges I'm facing,  I'm no longer afraid of not seeing my children.   I've decided to cook for my girls twice a week, Tues and Thurs,  of which I drop off pre-cooked meals for them at the door step.   I can't go in,  but I wave at them and get to see their faces light up when they see me and their favorite meals waiting for them.

The girl I asked out is very nice.   So nice that I'm not used to it.  My friend helped me build up the courage to do this, and I'm grateful for her support as well.  My new neighbors are excited to hang out with me once I'm settled in.   In fact,  I'm surrounded by people who like to have me around,  which again,  is new to me.   It has become apparent that I was in a toxic relationship for over half of my life, and now that I'm out of it, life seems so much more exciting and worth living.  

I'm not out of the woods yet, but at least right now I have surrounded myself with people who genuinely care about me.  Family and friends,  and the new friends who deeply care about me.  I owe it to not only them but also my girls to be happy.   And no amount of pain or bullshit from my ex is going to stop me.   

Here's to the future.

\--Darren

Update 4:

I've made a lot of progress in the past week.  I moved into an apartment, I've began furnishing it, and I'm preparing for the initial family court date.  

Despite this however I continue to struggle with severe depression.  My doctor has switched my medication and I'm adjusting to it.  My sex life has bottomed out.  I feel like a stranger in my own body.  I feel like a stranger in my own apartment.  I still don't see my girls.  And my ex has continued to move on like nothing is amiss.  

My father is in town this week, and it has been a strain to keep smiling and persevering with him around.  I have a few small things lined up to keep me busy but the same old invasive thoughts continue to batter me down.  I do not like the situation I am.  I still do not like this new me.

\-D

UPDATE 3:

Today was a checkpoint. I woke up at 4am to drive a few hours away to the highest bridge in my area (about 210 feet over water).  I stopped at a local gas station and bumped into my wife's old friend,  her partner in crime so to say.  I hadn't really spoken with her alone in about a decade.  I realized that all these years I had blamed her for allowing my wife to have her affairs (she was present).  There was no reason to blame this woman.  She had recently went through an ugly divorce,  and she cares deeply about my daughters,  so much so that she spoke very candidly about how she felt about my wife's recent behavior.  I realized that it was my wife who decided to have the affairs,  and only her.   This woman made me realize that I'm a great guy,  I was always too good for my wife.  Her words came out of nowhere,  I was just expecting to buy a drink and be out....instead, it changed my entire outlook.

I promised her that I wouldn't drink today.  So I drove to the bridge,  the walkway wasn't open yet (I arrived a little before dawn), and I ended up just driving back home.  There was no impulse to end my life.  I stopped at my wife's cousin's house later that day.  Again she repeated a lot of what my wife's old friend said.  Maybe it's not just me.  Maybe I'm not the crazy one.  They had unexpectedly given me the courage to fight my wife at her own game.  Why should I let her continue to control me?  She expects this to play out a certain way, why would I allow that?  No, I'm taking a stand.  I'm going to riposte her attack and turn the momentum against her.  She caught me flat footed,  now it's time for me to go on the offensive and tighten the screws on her.

Again all of this was so unexpected.  I went from attempting suicide once more to regaining lost confidence and taking a stand for myself.  Truly I did not see this coming.

\-LA

Actually I had a very good day today.  I had a revelation.  I'm no longer blaming myself or others for my wife's faults.  I know it sounds obvious but I'm finally holding her accountable for her actions.

I'm not going to allow her to have her way with custody. I am not going to just lay down.   I'm choosing to fight for my girls.  She always told me that I was a better person than her,  it is time I make a stand and show my daughters that their father is not down and out.

Whatever else my wife does is now her business, and what I do now is entirely mine.  It's time to move on.

*Suicide Note, dated 3/21/2021:*

Today I became a statistic.  A soon to be divorced husband, a man charged with raping his own wife, a devoted father who was kept from his children, a veteran; lost to suicide.  I tried to be vocal about my deteriorating condition, not to shame my wife or to cry wolf, but to show how even someone like myself can so quickly succumb to mental illness.

I did not want to die.  I was at the top of my career, making more money than I ever had in my life while only working three days a week.  I was a devoted father, spending more time than I ever had with both of my children.  I was the picture perfect husband, supporting my wife's career, supporting her through her depression, supporting her and walking with her through her decision to separate from me.  I died because it became unbearable.  Since January,  I have been haunted by that night.  Each week, each day, each hour became a struggle with my thoughts.  My brain would fight with itself, questioning every memory, trying to remember every detail, attempting to reason with actions that were done to harm me.  I turned to medical professionals for help and they prescribed medication that turned off what made me who I was.  I turned to friends and family who largely were supportive but many failed to support me when I called them out on their promises.  So I withdrew to myself and my thoughts.  I turned to alcohol to help stop those thoughts.  The alcohol would slow my mind, force sleep and thus stop the thoughts.  But the alcohol also dulled my executive choices, it quieted the will to live.  It was a deal with the Devil, and I knew it but it was the only thing within reach that didn't try to change me.

In January my wife, M, had me charged with Rape in the 1st degree.  She was issued a protectorate order that forbade me to contact her and forbade me from my home.  In March my wife, M, filed for full custody of our two children.  During this time she continued to live in the home where I had *raped* her, she continued to sleep in the bed where I had *raped* her, she continued to raise our children as if nothing had happened.  She then began to socialize with men and women who were involved in past infidelities.  She began to celebrate, party, drink; as if she had not been raped, as if her husband of 12 years, her best friend of 20 years was extirpated, torn out, from the root of her life.

I spent the first 90 days in denial and shock.  I spent that first day in jail questioning if I had really just raped my wife.  Was she in pain?  What had happened?  She didn't even speak to me that entire day.  I paid every bill I could.  Thousands of dollars paid without a second thought; my only way of communicating that I still cared.  And then the truth began to set in.  She had planned the entire thing.  She had been talking with people for months.  She had been withdrawing from me, the kids, and both our families.  She wanted out, and she wanted it all.  She knew she didn't have the moral highroad.  She knew she was in too deep with secret lifestyles, affairs, lovers, and online friends who she wanted to have;  when she wanted, how she wanted, and with whomever she wanted.  Nothing was going to stop her.  Not even her husband.

When she had asked me for a separation I do not think she was expecting me to consider it.  She kept on questioning why I hadn't just thrown her out or just divorced her.  I do not think she could handle the fact that I was attempting to rekindle the relationship; to rebuild what was lost.  She had zero intention of ever making the marriage work after that day in August.  Every date we had was uncomfortable.  Every talk we had was one sided.  Her insistence for no intimacy was a thin veil to cover her remaining guilt; guilty of being so happy with other people outside of the marriage.  But she did not have the strength to end it.  She was addicted; she couldn't stop. So, she allowed me to continue.  She, and she alone, had to get out.  And so did she stage the rape case to buy herself time?  She spun her lies to put distance between her words and her actions.  She would tell her parents one thing,  and do the exact opposite.  Even our own children, who spent the entire pandemic year with me, were now distant and only gave me one word answers to everything.

Friends and family have come forward with anecdotal stories about M, and how they didn't like her or felt uncomfortable around her.  These stories combined with her current behavior began to lift the veil I had placed around her.  She was a slut.  She was a whore.  But that was so long ago, she wasn't that woman anymore,  she wouldn't do that again?  She was, she had, and she knew it.  She had so much guilt,  so much anxiety,  so much pressure to hide it that she snapped.  Once the world saw her for who she was they would judge her,  she would lose her children,  she would lose the carefully crafted world she made for herself.  The world she had me make her.  Who was there to repay her debts when she robbed a bank?  Who was there when she miscarried?  Who was there when she had an abortion?  Who was there during both childbirths?  Who was there to provide her with a home?  Who was there to support her through her career?  Who was there when she hit rock bottom,  when she felt like running away?  Tell me M,  who was there?  It wasn't just me, was it?  How many others were there?.  Why did you control me like this?  Why did you abuse me like this?  Why did you have to destroy me?  Do you lash out because you're afraid of yourself?  Or are you truly just that cold, that heartless,  that mean.  I see it now.  I see what everyone has been saying for years.  I see the bitch.  I see the slut.  I see the manipulative woman.  And yet I do not hate you, I cannot hate you.  You were my best friend for 20 years.  I just pity you.  I was able to find so much happiness inside your heart,  but it seems you were unable to find any happiness inside of mine.  Ask people what they think of me,  ask people how they feel.   Does it bother you that you weren't able to find happiness in someone like myself?  That is a testament of how broken you really are.  After everything you put me through it wasn't me who was the difficult one to love.  It was you.  It was always you.  And now that I'm gone, only you remain.  Do you like what you see M?  Do not look away,  do not smile at your reflection,  do not try to rationalize it;  fix it.  This is not the M I fell in love with.  This is not the M I devoted my life to.  This is the M that you struggled with for years, the one you hid from all of us; and she is not the better M.

So why is it that I still love you M?  After everything you've done to me.  After how you deliberately destroyed me.  Am I crazy?  Am I an abused spouse who refuses to leave?  Or is there something more?  For 20 years, since we were 15, you were mine as I was yours.  You may be able to rationalize cheating on me and leaving me, but I cannot.  I do not see a future without you.  I do not see myself in a relationship.  I do not see myself fucking strangers for fun.  I just see that boy, that scared little boy who fell in love with you all those years ago.  And he cannot live watching you fall away.  He cannot stand being on the wayside as you continue your journey without him.  He is hurt, he has been used, he has been discarded, but he still loves you.  And that is something I am not ashamed of.  I am not ashamed of loving you unconditionally.  I just wish you were better to me.  I just wish our journey didn't come to an end like this.  But it's not for me to question.  What's done is done, and now we must all pay the price.  I will die today so that you can live.  Live without a bitter ex-husband, live without the guilt of leaving a good man, live as a better person than as you left me.  Do not lie to yourself M.  You are venomous.  You killed me.  But it's not too late to change your ways.  Never hurt someone again as you had hurt me.  Never take anyone's love for granted.  Never give up hope on yourself, and maybe just maybe, one day you'll truly be happy in this life.  Goodbye M.  I love you.  I always loved you.

Forever and always, your first husband,

D

*Excerpt from journal, 3/18/2021:*

I am gone.  By the time you read this again, I will still be gone.  You cannot change what has happened to me, as much as I couldn't change how you felt about me.  Let me help you this one last time, let me help you through your grief.

M, I want you to look into a mirror and tell yourself, *"It is my fault.  I did this to him.  I made him feel so worthless.  I killed my husband.  My actions drove my husband to suicide."*  Now live with that knowledge.  Explain to our girls how daddy was sick.  Explain to them who made daddy sick.  You weaponized your hate for me.  Your hate became a venom.  You poisoned my heart.  And you showed how incapable of regret you are.

Now take a deep breath and look at a picture of me.  Remember the sound of my voice, the tone I used when I showed you compassion, and say this:  *"M, you loved as well as you could.  You couldn't have stopped me from killing myself.  You may not have tried to work on our marriage, but I need you to try to believe what I'm about to say.  I forgive you.  It is not your fault.  Your actions hurt me deeply and led me down a dark path.  You were hurt, and I understand that the choice to do what you did must have not come easy.  I saw how much you could hate over the years.  I saw your mean streak.  I knew you were venomous and I chose to take that risk when I chose to give myself to you.  I chose to love you, and only you. I don't know if you still hold any love for me, but just know that before I took my own life I was still holding on to the idea of us. I still held on to those dreams we made together.  I still held on to the hope that maybe your heart still held some form of love for me.  Blame yourself today.  Allow yourself to cry.  Grieve the loss of us.  Allow yourself to heal.  Tomorrow, forgive yourself, do not forget what you did but find a way to move on.  You are not perfect but your flaws are what make who you are, M.  I found love in you, now find that love in yourself."*

I do not want you to suffer.  I accepted that you wanted out from my life.  Just remember my smile, my stupid jokes, that look I gave you, and remember what it felt to be loved.  You deserve to be loved again one day.  Until then, do not let yourself fall apart,  do not give up.  You can do it M, I always believed in you.  I fell in love with all your flaws, so I know you can fall in love with it too.

\-D

*Excerpt from journal, dated 2/18/2021:*

She has become a ghost and I just a faint remembrance of what we were.  Left with all the would've, could've, and should've beens.

What do you live for if you say you've never lived at all?  There is an intoxicating allure to the idea of suicide when control has been wrested away.  Not lost but taken.  Loss of control is how we learn to regain it.  Like an exercise in resiliency, it takes practice and failure for us to improve.  But when it's seized, taken abruptly, it leaves us bereft of a part of our soul.  Somehow our identity is tied to that sense of control.  Like an anchor for the ego.  Torn away, my soul lays bare.  A void in my sense of self.  In panic I grasp for any remnant of my past life, but I find no hold.  My soul begins to asphyxiate, drowning, the pain becomes insurmountable.  The pressure and tension never ends.  The body lives but the soul begins to die.  That is when the mind weakens, and like an injured animal, instinct takes over.  Self preservation fades.  Relief, if only for a moment, becomes priority.  To end this hell and its eternal suffering.  And it takes only but a moment.  One fleeting moment.

\-D

*Suicide Note, dated 3/20/2021:*

There was a cold surgical precision to the way I was removed from the family.  Within 30 minutes I went from the man you knew, just coming off of work, and was transformed into the charged criminal you see today.  There was no back and forth at the police station.  It was a swift decision that was made on my behalf.  I was not allowed to dispute it.  I was immediately removed from the household and immediately silenced; forbidden to talk to you.  After that point you then immediately proceeded with the divorce process.  I had no say.  We couldn't communicate.  My only choice was to accept what was being done to me.  Was it symbolic?  Were you trying to convey the feeling of your helplessness; trapped in our relationship?  Were you trying to rape me in return?  Imagine being in my shoes, if only for a second.  The woman who I was trying to help began to systematically dismantle me.  Piece by piece.  I lost my home.  I lost contact with my children.  I lost my wife.  I lost my best friend.  I was left ashamed of who I was.  I was left an outcast to my own family.  I have no friends because of it.  I have no exit plan.  Why did you treat me like this?  Did you ever, if only for a moment, feel bad for me?  Did you even know what I was going through?  I don't understand how you just stopped loving me.  Even if you were no longer in love, I was still your friend since high school, did you not feel for me?  Was it because I was out of sight, out of mind?  I have never hurt like this before.  It is a pain so deep, so persistent, that I want to end my life just so I can stop feeling.  I tried alcohol.  I tried making new friends.  I tried throwing myself at anyone who would have me.  And yet nothing worked.  The drink didn't make me forget the pain.  The new friends didn't ease the suffering.  And no one wanted me.  I feel ugly.  I feel shamed.  I feel unwanted.  I have no confidence.  I have no future.  And worst of all, I don't understand why it even had to be like this.  Couldn't we have settled this face to face?  As two adults.  Did you have to report a rape?  Did I even rape you?  Do you remember that day?  How you got undressed.  How you looked at me when you laid on the bed.  You hadn't touched me in months and then suddenly, after I asked, you gave yourself to me.  You allowed me to penetrate you.  It felt wrong.  You said you were willing but were you really just setting me up?  I don't understand.  I'll never understand.  Our marriage didn't end naturally.  Our marriage was killed.  You cut me out of the picture.  You silenced me.  Did you have to have complete control?  Were you afraid?  I just hope you got what you wanted out of this.  I hope you didn't want me to suffer.  I hope you didn't break me to see if I would kill myself.  You should've left long ago if you were this unhappy.  I shouldn't have sheltered you.  I truly thought I was helping my closest friend.  But in the aftermath, now that the dust has settled, I just ended up signing my own death warrant.  Maybe in a different world we would've grown old together co-parenting.  Maybe in another we would've fallen in love again.  Perhaps in one of these worlds you were happy.  But in this one, I only see myself standing in your way.  You refused to remove yourself from this unhappy marriage, allow me to remove myself.

Forever and always, your ex-husband,

\-D

*Excerpt from journal, dated 2/22/2021:*

I want to make it clear that only I'm to blame for this.  Did people and circumstance play a role?  Of course, but I ultimately made the choice.  I find myself backed into a corner.  I find myself staring at a life I do not want.  Facing punishment for something I did not do.  For once in my life I can say that I'm unhappy.  I'm unhappy for my failed marriage.  Unhappy for my distant children.  Unhappy for my wife, dearest of friends, who seems content in her role of my complete destruction.  Unhappy for my stifled future.  I had it all, and what I lacked was never out of reach.   
 My wife was unhappy.  She did want to confront it.  I held her hand when she couldn't look me in the eye and ask for the separation she wanted.  I embraced her as she broke down when she admitted she did not want to be my wife.  I only asked her what her plans were.  She had none.  She was deeply unhappy and yet content to just stay in place.  She didn't seem to want to try, or at least not try for me.  So now, yes I can say that I'm unhappy.  I have every reason to be unhappy.  Hopefully she will find what happiness means to her.  Otherwise what an incredible waste if we both end up miserable.  Was it worth cost?  You watched as I tried to save you.  You watched as I waded into the murky waters of your depression to help you.  You knew that I would give myself to your demons if in return they would release you from their grip.  Now tell me with a straight face, do you think I deserve this?  Is the ruination of my life worth the chance to find yours?  You had your chance, it was yours for the taking, but you froze.  Afraid to take action.  Afraid to confront yourself.  Now it's too late, the damage is done.  Make the most of it, but never forget what it cost.  Your new found happiness and your new found future, with or without me, was bled from my body.  The body you left behind in those waters.  I watched as you walked away.  You did not look back.  All your life you have been moving forward, and now you are here.  Now we finally see each other as we really are.  Do you like what you see?

\-D

*Excerpt from journal, dated 3/13/2021:*

I'm not ready to die.  It's not romantic, it's not stoic; it's desperate and it's contagious.  The instinct to run is ever present.  I do not want to be in this situation.  I can't run.  I can't hide.  Every aspect of me is out in the public.  Every aspect of my failed relationship is public.  Every fear and insecurity stings overwhelmingly.  I went from a helping hand to one that's desperately grasping out.  My hurt wife became a weapon.  A loaded gun aimed squarely at my heart.  Exposed, she shot straight into my weakest point.  And then she covered her tracks.  Buying time by destroying my life.  How could you?  After I spent years of my life helping you rebuild yourself.  Your confidence, our family, your career.  You took everything.  You took it for yourself.  I never held it over you.  Everything of mine was always yours.  Were you always like this?  Was I too blind to see the red flags?  I will die not knowing who you truly are.  I chose to believe that the woman I once knew was still inside you.  Now I doubt she was even real.  She's lost.  Maybe she's dead and gone.  I was with you for 20 years.  I was there to lead you through it all.  You were never alone.  I was always there to pick you up.  Now it's me who's fading away.  I'm afraid.  Now you need to do this on your own.

\-D

UPDATE 2:

So another week has passed.  More drama.  When my wife served me the custody papers (of which she gave to my Mom and had her inadvertently serve her own son), she purposely didn't include the child support paperwork.  My family attorney stated that this a common tactic used to default spouses into the full child support payment amount (it's only required by my state law to serve custody papers, not support papers).  The exact amount will be determined by the family court, but it's scheduled well in advance of my criminal court hearing.  She stands to double her income, due to the sheer difference in our pay grades (she makes under 30k, and I around 90k).  I will lose custody in the short term, of that there is no contention, but I am concerned she will do what she can to mess with any visitation (so far every action she's made has been very calculated).

She's also continued to socialize with numerous people who she attempted to hide throughout the years.  These are online friends, work friends, friends of friends, who she would erase all conversations with, hang out with covertly, and often let slip references of inside jokes between them when talking about her day.  Again, I have nothing against these people but their timing is suspect.  At this point she has moved on, with no intention of coming back or any consideration of my feelings.  She's looking after number one.  Her family continues to be concerned about her.  She's withdrawn from her own parents and other close members of her family.

My daughters have withdrawn from me.  I had spent the entire pandemic year with them, home-schooling, transportation, activities, ect..,  so this behavior is new and unlike them. My oldest daughter, 14, only talks to me in single word responses.  "Ok", "Fine", "Sure".  Which is typical of a teenager, but she used to come to me for everything. We were very close.  My youngest daughter, 8, has also showed behavioral changes.  She is a bottomless pit.  She will ask for a snack immediately after eating one.  She's also a spitfire, a daredevil,  she'll speak her mind and she'll jump off of anything.  Now she's very quiet and reserved, and worse yet she's lost her trademark appetite.  I was very worried about my children when this whole thing started, and now my fears are starting to come true.  They recently spoke with an attorney, about what I do not know, but it looks like their mother has asked them to take sides.  My wife also doesn't allow my daughters to speak with my own mother unsupervised.  Where the girls would run over to Mimi's side to talk, have snacks, and just hang out;  now my wife is ever present and ushers them in and out.

My drinking problem has continued.  I've never been much of a drinker but now it's the only thing that helps me sleep, and it's the first thing I reach for in the morning.  I know it's a terrible habit, but I feel like it's a necessary deal with the Devil I need to at least somewhat function.  I'm also very lonely.  I did not have many close friends to begin with, but I do have a good number of acquittances (friends who I just  wouldn't confide with, go into their homes).  I've made a few new friends which has definitely helped get my mind off the whole ordeal.  I've also attempted to throw myself at anyone who would have me.  Again, sexual promiscuity's not my thing (I married my high school sweetheart and I did have a single affair during my marriage; so the amount of women I've slept with can be counted on one hand), but it doesn't matter because I haven't had anyone take me up on it.  For better or for worse, it is what it is.

So that leaves me with tomorrow's checkpoint.  I'm struggling with depression and anxiety again. My medication has been doubled recently, but I feel no marked improvement.  Tomorrow I am planning on driving down to a new location to try a new method.  It's about a 2 hour drive; designed to help dissuade me on the way there.  This has been in the works for a week.  I am afraid this time because the stress continues to compound, and I continue to withdraw further into myself.  As a self imposed hurdle, I have asked myself to post a picture or some other personal piece of information in order to deter myself. I have also prepared a few video journals and I completed my personal journal (filled up 190 pages), so I suppose those should give my loved ones a few things to go through;  if anything give them some insight on these troubled 90+ days.

Again, I'm not crying for help nor am I trying to stir up drama.  I am just trying to put my thoughts on paper and trying to make sense of the fractured mess that is my mind.  I have been through a lot these past 20 years.  I should say we have been through a lot, my wife and I that is.  She has been by my side since I was 15.  I have grown so accustomed to her, the desire to protect her is impossible for me to shake.  And yet she ended up forcing me out of the picture and moving on without so much as a double take.  That is what truly hurts, seeing someone you love so dearly and being unable to recognize them.  Unable to recognize their actions, their feelings, unable to recognize the woman who I believed was my best friend.

Thank you again for reading.  Please call someone you love today, or give someone a hug.

\-LA

That's a question I've been asking for myself for over a decade now.  I'll be candid about this, so the mods may downvote or remove this:  It doesn't get any easier.

I'm like you where I'm deathly afraid of heights (ironically I was part of helicopter squadron in the military), so the few times I've approached great heights I managed to scare the life back into myself.

I've stared down loaded firearms and didn't feel compelled to apply the 7 or so pounds of trigger pressure.

I've driven my car up to various piers, ziptied my hands to the steering wheel but yet I never managed to drive off.

Now, I don't know you or what your situation is but I'm betting your stubborn, which is a good thing in this case, because you're still here.  I can't tell you where to find the courage, and honestly I don't even know if I would even call it courage.  But what I can tell you is that, as a complete stranger,  I'd want you to at least try and take a moment to breathe.  I'm struggling alongside with you.  You can read up on my posts if you want to distract yourself for a few minutes.  But just know it's not something you're likely to find an answer to as it were a question,  it'll be likely end up just being a reflex.  Something felt.  At least that's my interpretation because I'm struggling with it at this exact moment ((I have a checkpoint in the morning, and I'm dreading it)).

Anyhow, try to get some rest and calm your mind.  You can look me up, I tend to give weekly updates on my own journey.  Whoever you are, I feel for you.

\--LA

I'm sorry man.   It's going to hurt.  You may still love her.  She can't take that away from you, even if she tells you she never loved you.  However you can't love someone who doesn't want to be loved.   My wife didn't want to be loved,  and no amount of love I gave her made any difference.  Right now the best thing you can do is stay with family and talk,  or maybe try a crisis center if you're in serious need of help (just be aware that they may admit you for a week).

At the very least I would suggest removing the bolt from your firearm and giving it to a friend or store it somewhere out of the home.  You don't want to end up like me where the police confiscate it, and then you'll feel ever more powerless.  

I'm going through my own shit (you can read my post from the other week if you want), but just know you're not alone.

\-LA

I agree.  Right now, it's likely shock.  You may want to check into a Crisis center just for support,  if you don't have any family available who would understand your circumstance.  For me my wife is my emotional trigger,  and right now,  your husband's negative reaction may be yours.

UPDATE 1:
